m_dialogEntries.m_dialog: Stinger Bell? I might be him, I might not. What's it to you, Spellbinder? Your Goliath friend wants the Scrolls of War, huh?
I heard the Night Flame captain, Ullek EmberTongue, declared the Scrolls works of treason, and took them to Camp Havoc.
But being labeled a traitor would be bad for my business. So if you want the Scrolls of War, you'll have to get them yourself.
Now, this information isn't free. If you do manage to get the Scrolls, tell your Goliath friend he owes me a favor. Got it?
Every Scroll of War is here! How did Stinger Bell manage to get them all?
What? You had to fight Ullek EmberTongue for them? What did he want with them?
Well, He clearly learned nothing from them if he tried to fight you!
As the very first line of the first Scroll of War says, <ITALICS>The wise warrior avoids battle. </ITALICS>
The Scrolls also say no good deed goes unpunished. I owe favors to Stinger and you. Come see me if you ever need tactical advice.
:tik: Greetings, Spellbinder. Might I trouble you for a bit of your time? :tik:
Before my assignment in the Weeping Tower, I was a guard in the Athenaeum, which housed the Burrower's ancient Scrolls of War.
I would sneak Scrolls down to read when no one was looking. Over time, I was able to educate myself on a myriad of subjects.
Then one day the Umbra Legion declared all Burrower literature treasonous, and confiscated every Scroll in the Athenaeum.
There is great knowledge in those Scrolls. I want to finish the Scrolls of War, but there's no way I can get permission from my Umbra Legion superiors.
I've heard there's a Yellow Jacket who can attain the unattainable. But he's in the Moon Cliffs, and I can't leave my post here
His name is Stinger Bell. Can you find him and ask him to procure the Scrolls of War for me? Please, whatever it takes. :tik:.
:tik: Ask Stinger Bell if he can procure the Scroll of War for me. I'll do whatever it takes!
